Specifically, our approach utilizes Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) for cryptography, Diffie-Hellman for secure key exchange, and Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) steganography to ensure robust data security. AES encrypts the data, making it unreadable to unauthorized users, while Diffie-Hellman for secure key exchange ensures robust protection against unauthorized access. The encrypted data is then hidden within digital images using DCT steganography, adding an extra layer of security. This dual approach aims to reduce the risks of data breaches, unauthorized access, and tampering. Our proposed method demonstrates high effectiveness in maintaining data confidentiality, integrity, and availability without severely impacting system performance, highlighting the potential of this combined strategy in safeguarding cloud-stored data. Performance metrics analysis shows our approach is robust and efficient, ensuring enhanced protection for cloud-based data.

articleTitle: EEG Transmission Over 6G Using Optimized Pilot-Based Channel Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: Electroencephalogram signals are crucial for telemedicine applications, demanding reliable and real-time transmission. This paper proposes an efficient EEG signal transmission system leveraging the high bandwidth and low latency capabilities of 6G wireless networks. Accurate channel estimation is vital for reliable data recovery in wireless EEG transmission. This work employs a pilot-based channel estimation technique optimized for EEG signal characteristics. By optimizing pilot symbol placement and utilizing advanced estimation algorithms, the proposed system achieves high channel estimation accuracy, leading to improved signal quality at the receiver. Simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed system in achieving reliable and efficient EEG signal transmission over 6G networks, paving the way for enhanced telemedicine applications.

articleTitle: Next-Generation Wearable Antenna: Optimized Multi-Band Performance for Advanced Wireless Systems and Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: The escalating demand for advanced wearable technology necessitates the seamless integration of communication systems into daily life. This paper discusses the creation and assessment of a high-performance multiband wearable antenna designed for advanced wireless systems and future wearable applications. The proposed antenna, with dimensions of 47 x 30 x 1.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, operates across an extensive frequency range of 2.35-3.57 GHz and 4.97-10.45 GHz. Through numerous design iterations, significant improvements have been made in critical performance metrics, including a peak gain of 6.5 dB, impedance bandwidths of 41.22% and 71.10%, and radiation efficiency exceeding 70%. The specific absorption rate (SAR) is maintained at a safe level of 0.45 W/ kg. Thorough testing under bending conditions and in close proximity to the human body confirmed the resilience and effectiveness of the antenna in practical situations. A comparative analysis reveals that the proposed antenna outperforms existing designs in terms of size, frequency coverage, gain, SAR, and efficiency, making it a superior option for modern wearable wireless communication devices.

articleTitle: Network Analysis of Multisource Packet Capture Files Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: The study uses machine learning methods to identify and detect Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks. The dataset used in this research was captured from the Packet capture (PCAP) files of the CTU-13, CIC-DDoS2019, and CIC-DoS2017 datasets, which contain different kinds of DDoS attacks such as ICMP, UDP, TCP, and HTTP flooding. Data features were extracted from attack packets classified using time windows, with the packet windows being of different lengths to correct the distribution of packets into the classes. Network analysis helps conceptualize and solve DDoS-related problems by analyzing traffic. To detect DDoS attacks, the proposed systems use machine learning classifiers: Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, K-NN (K5), XGBoost (XGB), and Light GBM (LGBM). The investigation of the ‘PKT_COUNT’ attribute led to a positive correlation and subsequent feature selection process, while only outliers were ‘cleaned out’ to yield higher gains in model accuracy. The target variable ‘PKT_COUNT’ was then transformed into a binary form to detect the analyzed malware easily. To create a robust model, significant efforts were made to clean the dataset with processing, such as detecting and removing the outliers, ensuring the model's reliability. The analysis of models was assessed concerning the area under the Receiver Operating Characteristic - Accuracy (ROC-AUC), mean Average Precision (AP), and Accuracy Scores. Therefore, the novel machine learning-based system presented in this paper introduces a robust method of DDoS attack detection that overcomes the drawbacks of existing steps to analyze network traffic. The study raises the possibility of developing more sophisticated classifiers to be incorporated into an environment to optimize DDoS attack detection and improve network security.

articleTitle: A Surrogate Approach to Explainable AI for Predictive Maintenance: Techniques and Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: Predictive maintenance is a process that utilizes machine-learning models to predict equipment failure or maintenance needs, thus enabling proactive interventions and optimizing operational costs. However, these models often lack transparency and act as black boxes that provide predictions without explanation. Trust, safety, and compliance are hampered by this opacity, particularly in vital applications like manufacturing, aviation, and energy. In order to overcome this difficulty, explainable AI (XAI) approaches improve the interpretability and transparency of machine-learning algorithms and offer insights into how they make decisions. This paper presents a comprehensive framework for applying XAI to predictive maintenance, and explores various techniques and their applications. The techniques investigated included feature importance, model interpretability, visual explanations, and counterfactual explanations. These techniques were evaluated on a real-world dataset, demonstrating their effectiveness in interpreting predictions, identifying influential factors, and providing actionable insights into maintenance decisions. The tradeoffs between interpretability and model accuracy are also covered in this work, along with the difficulties and potential paths for further research in this area.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Adder Topologies Integrated into MAC Units and MLP Model for Digit Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: Multilayer perceptron (MLP) is a variant of deep neural networks often used in handwritten digit classification and recognition. Conventional processors, such as CPUs and GPUs, encounter computational challenges with the increasing complexity of MLP models, and ASIC development is time-consuming. This work aims to enhance MLP prediction algorithms using FPGA-based Multiply and Accumulate (MAC) arrays. FPGAs offer a promising alternative due to their flexibility and hardware acceleration potential. An RTL was designed using Verilog HDL in Xilinx Vivado to perform MAC operations for the MLP module with a multiple processing element (PE) MAC array, synthesized on the ZCU-104 FPGA. Various adder topologies including ripple carry adder (RCA), carry select adder (CSelA), and carry look-ahead adder (CLA), were incorporated into the PEs. The MLP model, trained and tested on the MNIST dataset, achieves an accuracy of 97.6%. The 64 PE model can classify 10,100 images per second with 96.5% accuracy using 32-bit fixed-point numbers. The CSelA-based MAC array demonstrates a 32.33% reduction in computational delay compared to RCA, making it ideal for high-speed hardware accelerators.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Prediction of Depression in Medical Fielders with CES-D Using MPF Method
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: Stress acts as a normal reaction given to outside forces from obligations that may trigger sensations like nervousness, worry, even overload. Depression being another increased one, continuous psychological disease that involves intense lowness, desolation, often losing curiosity or enjoyment towards the hobbies. These two disorders have considerable effects on someone's routine including general health. Mood disorders around people in the medical industry frequently result in decreased career success, higher incorrect diagnosis, along with exhaustion within those who practice medicine. Certain personality disorders may contribute to increased desertion and attrition reducing entire effectiveness with efficacy concerning medical treatment. Also, persistent mood disorders could negatively impact psychological wellness even work-life balance among physicians, potentially threatening all over medical fielders flexibility. The psychological state of physicians can be assessed using the Multilayered Progressive Formulation method (MPF), which involves translating information as distributed design while discovering separate groups using resemblance measurements. This strategy efficiently exposes similarities with clusters, allowing for a classification for different psychological states. This enhanced Classification detects the various levels of stress and depression with the people in the medical sector, achieving an accuracy of 86% and precision score as 0.86, recall score 0.85 and F1 score as 0.86. The developed classification method gives a well performance of multilayered progressive and achieving better accuracy and performance metrics.

articleTitle: Design of Microstrip Patch Antenna Using Support Vector Regression
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: Microstrip patch antennas are popular due to their compact size, lightweight nature, cost-effectiveness, and ease of fabrication, making them suitable for applications like mobile devices and satellite communications where size, performance, and cost are crucial. However, optimizing these antennas for desired performance metrics such as bandwidth, gain, and efficiency presents challenges, as traditional design methods often require time-consuming iterative processes and extensive simulations. To address these challenges, Support Vector Regression is employed to predict the design parameters, specifically the antenna's length and width, to achieve a desired resonant frequency and gain. In this approach, data is gathered using an HFSS simulation tool by varying the patch's width and length. This simulation data serves as the training set for the SVR model, which is then evaluated for its predictive accuracy. The trained SVR model is applied to predict the patch dimensions at a resonant frequency of 2.35 GHz. These predicted dimensions are subsequently used to design the antenna in HFSS, where simulation results show a return loss of -18.3 dB and a gain of 3.2 dB at 2.35 GHz. Comparing the SVR model's predictions with the HFSS simulation outcomes reveals that while the gain values are relatively close, the HFSS simulation yields a significantly lower return loss, indicating better performance than the SVR model predictions.

articleTitle: Enhanced Electronic Diagnosis System by CCNNViT Model for Kidney Cyst Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: A major health issue for kidney failure is becoming worse due to changes in diet, obesity, underlying medical conditions, mineral deficiencies. The kidneys calculus, also known as kidney cysts, is a hard accumulation of nutrients from the stool that develops in the urinary tract. One method of imaging that medical professionals use to diagnose kidney cysts is computerized tomography (CT). Kidney cysts are sometimes difficult to identify with the unaided eye owing to the poor quality that produces these images, which could result in false alarms. In order to help clinicians with diagnosis, an advanced deep learning technique-based electronic diagnosis system has been built throughout this work. Kidney cysts can be identified by CNN based deep learning algorithms. until now, it has issues with the conventional implementation and the efficiency of the convolution operations performed in the convolution layers. The suggested deep learning architecture uses a hybrid approach as a combination of CNN and pooling vision transformer (CCNNViT) technique that is incorporated in the deep learning architecture to decrease characteristic map redundant employment without the convolution overlap. We propose a method that extracts stated and abstract characteristics from the input pictures, thereby improving the network's efficiency. The suggested architecture is developed using the kidney cysts CT scans that are made accessible to anyone on Kaggle. Using CT scans, our automated simulation identified kidney cysts with a 98.9% accuracy rate. Our method outperforms some of the most recent and modern techniques for detecting kidney cysts of any form, even the tiniest previous ones. The present research proposes an innovative method for detecting cysts in the kidneys that uses Pooling-based Vision Transformers (PiT) and excludes the uterus from the evaluation.

articleTitle: Hybridization of a Single-Phase Induction Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: Energy saving has been a challenge for decades. The conventional solution to this problem has been to manage it at the generation or distribution end. In any household, there is always some power lost during the conversion from AC to DC and vice versa. Therefore, rather than trying to increase conversion efficiency to address this problem, with this project sought to eliminate the conversion process. The concept of a DC home, in which PV panels feed DC power to homes directly is becoming increasingly popular. However, this DC power further undergoes a conversion to AC before being supplied to any household appliance. If the load is DC, this AC power is again converter to DC through a front-end rectifier built in the appliance. An increasing number of appliances are of DC loads today; phones, laptops, TVs, gadgets, light bulbs, etc. This leads to a lot of conversion losses in operating a conventional single-phase induction motor. Therefore, the goal of this research is to hybridize i.e., to enable a SPIM to operate on both AC and DC power, allow the SPIM to be self-starting and control the motor speed using V/f control.

articleTitle: Enhancing Feature Selection with PSO-RK-Gaussian Algorithm for Cancer Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: The PSO-RK-Gaussian algorithm enhances traditional Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) by integrating Runge-Kutta (RK) numerical methods and Gaussian sampling techniques, specifically to improve feature selection in complex biomedical datasets. PSO uses a population of potential solutions called particles, with each particle representing a candidate solution within the search space. These particles iteratively adjust their positions based on two main factors: their own best-known positions (local best) and the best-known positions of the entire swarm (global best). This dual adjustment allows the particles to navigate toward promising regions within the search space, effectively balancing exploration and exploitation to find optimal solutions. Our enhanced method demonstrates clear superiority over traditional PSO and other baseline techniques in both feature selection quality and predictive modelling accuracy. Through rigorous experimentation, the PSO-RK-Gaussian algorithm shows significant improvements in key evaluation metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC-ROC. These results underscore the algorithm's potential for applications in bioinformatics, particularly for analysing large and complex biomedical datasets. Additionally, our method provides a robust framework that can be adapted to various optimization problems beyond bioinformatics. This adaptability and the demonstrated improvements in predictive modelling suggest a broad applicability of the PSO-RK-Gaussian algorithm across different domains requiring efficient and effective feature selection.

articleTitle: Automated Extraction from Aerospace Engineering Diagrams Using Computer Vision Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: Aerospace engineering design and manufacturing greatly rely on accurate and efficient plane wing diagram data extraction. This paper introduces an innovative technique for automating the process using state-of-the-art computer vision approaches. Cutting edge image processing technologies extract vital technical metrics from these schematics. Experimental results demonstrate this methodology extracts information approximately four times faster than human input and with considerably higher precision. Improved design workflows and dependable engineering results are encouraged by such a feature. Collectively, these initiatives moreover offer insight into how computer vision may revive outdated methods in aeronautical engineering. Streamlined yet trustworthy design processes and results are made possible through such automated and precise data extraction from schematics. Meanwhile, revived methods hold potential to re-energize the field and ensure continued advancement.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Various Deep Learning Models in Lung Cancer Detection and Classification Using Medical Images
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: Lung cancer remains a prevalent and deadly disease, accounting for millions of deaths globally each year. Early detection and accurate diagnosis of lung cancer are pivotal in improving patient outcomes and survival rates. Traditional diagnostic methods often face limitations in sensitivity and specificity, necessitating the exploration of advanced technological solutions. This research paper explores the application of deep learning models, specifically Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), ResNet50, MobileNetV2 and VGG-16 architectures, in the detection and classification of lung cancer from medical imaging data. The primary objective of this study is to develop and evaluate deep learning-based models capable of identifying lung cancer patterns in radiological images, notably X-rays and CT scans. These models leverage the inherent capacity of deep learning to automatically extract intricate features and patterns from complex image data, aiding in the precise identification of cancerous regions. The paper reviews the strengths and limitations of existing approaches examining their efficacy in identifying and classifying lung nodules in achieving reliable and robust results. Furthermore, it addresses the challenges associated with utilizing deep learning in medical diagnosis, such as data scarcity, bias, and interpretability. Through meticulous analysis and experimentation, we aim to evaluate the potential of deep learning models to revolutionize lung cancer detection, paving the way for improved patient outcomes and early intervention strategies.

articleTitle: Area and Power Optimized RTL to GDS II Flow of a Telecommunication Receiver Core
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: The Register Transfer Level (RTL) to Graphic Design System II (GDS II) flow is pivotal in any integrated circuit (IC) design. The work outlines the process of IC design from RTL to GDS II, leveraging Cadence EDA tools: Genus for logic synthesis and Innovus for physical design implementation. As a case study, a telecommunication receiver core implemented using Verilog code is considered. Key components of the receiver core are a phase-locked loop for clock generation, a signal processing core for real-time signal processing, and a power manager for efficient distribution. These are essential for telecommunication signal decoding in applications such as telephone dialing and interactive voice response systems. The paper aims at optimizing design parameters for performance, area, and power, ensuring reliability and meeting application demands. The synthesis step transforms high-level descriptions into gate-level representations, optimizing for various metrics, while physical design implementation ensures efficient placement, routing, and clock distribution. Evaluation of timing and power characteristics facilitates cost reduction and chip area optimization. The study proposes optimization of area, timing, and power. The optimization results emphasize a reduction in cell area by 1730 um<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, an increase in positive slack value by 33%, and a total power reduction of 25%. All optimization techniques were implemented using Cadence's Genus and Innovus.

articleTitle: Small Object Detection for UAVs Using Deep Learning Models on Edge Computing: A Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis of DNN-models, including TensorFlow Lite, SSD-MobileNet, Mask R-CNN and YOLOv8, for the high-precision detection and classification of small objects in aerial search and rescue scenarios. The study features a proprietary dataset collected through drone flights over an extended period. The model performance was evaluated on compact computing platforms like Jetson Nano and Raspberry Pi, emphasizing detection accuracy and computational efficiency. Results reveal trade-offs between model complexity and real-time processing capabilities. The findings guide the selection of on-board computer models, thereby enhancing drone capabilities in critical operations

articleTitle: Cancer Detection Using MEMS Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: Cancer is a chronic illness marked by reduced immunity as a result of the body's cellular deterioration. In the later stages, this may prove to be harmful and cause long-term damage and organ failure. The process of making a medical diagnosis can be challenging and filled with uncertainty. Variations in symptoms can result in different diagnoses. For the early detection of cancer, a variety of invasive and non-invasive techniques are available. Some can detect in its early stages, but are expensive, prone to human error and time consuming. The demand for non-invasive method has grown which does not involve any machinery. MEMS is a non-invasive method for the detection of cancer and is efficient with the results as it includes microstructures and nanotechnology structures. Here, use of a microcantilever structure with various designs to detect the presence of cancer is discussed for different types of cancers. Based on the deflection of the cantilever, various types of cancer can be detected. Piezoelectric material has been included for the microcantilever structure to detect cancer. Another method implemented for detecting cancer is a temperature sensor with a micro-probe. Both these approaches have been simulated and the results show that these devices can be fabricated and tested. These methods present real-time, quick, effective, and accurate diagnosis.

articleTitle: Advancements in Brain Tumor Segmentation Using Modified UNet Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: The ability to segment brain tumors from MRI images is essential for enhancing prognosis, treatment planning, and diagnosis. Manual segmentation is labor-intensive and varies significantly between radiologists, making automated methods essential. This study presents a comprehensive analysis and implementation of various U-Net-based brain tumor segmentation architectures. We explored Vanilla U-Net, U-Net with ResNeXt50 backbone, Feature Pyramid Network (FPN), and an enhanced U-Net model incorporating attention mechanisms and Edge Enhancing Diffusion (EED) filtering. Our models were trained and evaluated using public datasets. The models demonstrated significant improvements in segmentation accuracy, with the best-performing model achieving a Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) of 97.642 %, Train Loss of 0.219, Validation Loss of 0.216, Train DICE of 0.808, and Validation DICE of 0.977. These results underscore the potential of advanced U-Net architectures in improving brain tumor detection precision and effectiveness segmentation, providing a reliable tool for aiding radiologists in clinical settinos.

articleTitle: Voice Controlled Moving Robot for Smart Surveillance
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: Smart surveillance robots are autonomous or semi-autonomous systems designed for advanced security applications, equipped with sensors, cameras, and monitoring technologies. These robots provide real-time monitoring, detect threats, and respond proactively, thereby reducing the need for human intervention and lowering operational costs. They employ sophisticated algorithms to identify objects, recognize faces, and track individuals or items of interest, making them effective in areas such as public safety, industrial monitoring, and home security. By continuously analyzing data from multiple sensors, these robots can detect anomalies, prevent unauthorized access, and ensure uninterrupted surveillance. Their autonomous navigation capabilities allow them to patrol large, complex areas without direct human control, ensuring comprehensive coverage and rapid response to potential threats. As a result, smart surveillance robots offer a cost-effective solution for continuous security and asset protection, providing reliable, around-the-clock safety management with minimal human oversight.

articleTitle: Slimmer Deep Learning Architectures for Drone Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: The increasing risk posed by the use of drones in illicit activities has made drone detection crucial for security and surveillance. This task, however, faces challenges such as false alerts caused by birds or distant appearances. In this context, You Only Look Once (YOLO) based algorithms, and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have demonstrated exceptional effectiveness in detecting and classifying drones and birds. Despite their effectiveness, deploying CNN models on edge devices is challenging due to memory limitations and resource-intensive demands, necessitating compression approaches like knowledge distillation and pruning. Pruning reduces memory storage requirements by eliminating unnecessary weights from the model, decreasing the model size and making it suitable for resource-constrained environments. However, this often leads to reduced accuracy. To mitigate this loss, knowledge distillation is employed. Various CNN architectures, including ResNet50, ResNet101,ResNet50v2, DenseNet121, Inceptionv3, and VGG16 are utilized with pruning and knowledge distillation. A custom dataset with 1000 drone images and 1000 bird images is considered for evaluation and the results indicate that slimmer versions of DenseNet121 and ResNet50v2, after pruning and knowledge distillation, achieved higher accuracy of 99% and 99.25%, respectively with inference speeds of 0.93s and 0.89s, respectively, on a Tesla T4 GPU. These results highlight the potential of deploying high-performance, compact CNNs on edge devices for real-time drone detection.

articleTitle: Aquify:AI-Enhanced Predictive Analytics Toolkit For Water Contamination
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: Effective monitoring of water quality remains a problem, in real-time contamination detection and prediction. Despite advancements in the sector, many existing approaches continue to rely on labor-intensive laboratory testing, which limits their capacity to give rapid and accurate results. By leveraging advanced ML/DL models, it is possible to build a more robust and adaptable platform for real-time analysis, prediction, and decision support. Approaches based on models such as Random Forest, XGBoost, CNN, RNN, LSTM, and GRU have been good with the accuracy of water quality predictions. They help identify pollution sources and diagnose water quality issues, providing essential information to stakeholders in sustainable water resource management. The ML and DL approaches help improve water quality monitoring and boost future research in environmental sustainability and natural resource management.

articleTitle: A Clustering Approach on Unveiling Global Development Disparities
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: This paper seeks to go further and use clustering, hypothesis testing as well as attribute independence analysis to delve deeper into the world development indicators such as birth rate, infant mortality, business taxes rates etc., in a bid to pinpoint key relationships in the underlying socio-economic environment of the world today. Regional classifications, based on socio- economic development indicators, show that there are groupings of countries with similar development characteristics and this makes it easier to review, and analyze regional disparities. Hypothesis testing allows us to determine if there is indeed a correlation, such as between the business tax rates and Gross domestic product [GDP] growth or spending on health care and life expectancy. Also, the interdependence and the extent of the impact of these factors may be determined by identifying how precisely each component correlates with the others. And comparative analysis of these indicators were performed using the clustering techniques such as K means, hierarchical clustering, Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise [DBSCAN] and Spectral. The silhouette score for the clusters using K means and Hierarchical clustering shows up better analysis of the development status of the countries based on the world development features.

articleTitle: Predictive Analysis of Plant Macronutrient Consumption Pattern Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: This study incorporates many machine learning (ML) methods to predict and analyze the nutrient intake as it explores the macronutrient consumption patterns of different plants in few different states of India. Important macronutrient factors for a wide variety of plant species were recorded using data gathered from a variety of agricultural online sources. Creating precise prediction models to improve nutrition management strategies was the main goal. K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Naive Bayes, and Support Vector Classification (SVC) were the three machine learning techniques used. Based on how well these algorithms predicted intake of macronutrients, their performance was assessed. The outcomes showed that, at 95.87%, Naive Bayes had the best accuracy, followed by KNN at 89.65% and SVC at 83.85%. Our results demonstrate that Naive Bayes is the best appropriate machine learning approach for this dataset analysis and show its promise for efficient nutrition prediction. Finally, by promoting sustainable farming practices, this research helps optimise nutrient management systems

articleTitle: RISC-V Architecture based Hardware Accelerator for kNN
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: The demand for smarter devices has pushed embedded systems to their limits, particularly in computationally intensive tasks like image recognition and natural language processing. Hardware accelerators have emerged as a solution, offering significant performance and energy efficiency gains. However, traditional accelerators tied to specific processor architectures suffer from limitations like reduced flexibility and vendor lock-in. This project proposes a hardware accelerator for the K-Nearest Neighbor (kNN) algorithm, leveraging the open-source RISC-V architecture. RISC-V addresses the computational complexity, performance bottlenecks, and energy efficiency challenges of existing kNN implementations. The accelerator is designed with key features such as a customized instruction set, parallelism, pipelining, reduced power consumption, and optimized area utilization. The project aims for efficient use of flip-flops (FFs) and look-up tables (LUTs), ensuring optimal resource utilization.By utilizing RISC-V's flexibility, this project aims to create an efficient hardware accelerator for kNN, enabling real-time processing of large datasets, minimizing energy use, and ensuring scalability across different applications.

articleTitle: Medical Imaging: Denoising with Discrete Fourier Transform, Clustering, and Statistical Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: In the complex realm of medical imaging, noise poses a significant challenge as every pixel can convey crucial information that might save lives. Various factors, including environmental noise, sensor noise, and the intrinsic constraints of imaging equipment, can cause denoising in images. This study introduces a novel image denoising approach specifically applied to the Alzheimer's dataset, which is crucial for understanding and diagnosing Alzheimer's disease. The dataset comprises five distinct classes, each representing different stages or types of the disease, making it particularly significant in the medical field. Theproposed method leverages a combination of Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT), Inverse Discrete Fourier Transform (IDFT), Butterworth low-pass filtering, and Non-local Means denoising to enhance image quality. By employing Fourier Transform, the study performs frequency domain analysis on the image data, enabling the extraction of vital information while reducing noise. Furthermore, K-means clustering is used to categorize noisy and denoised images based on visual similarities. To validate the effectiveness of the denoising technique, statistical evaluations are conducted through hypothesis testing, comparing noise levelsand quality metrics between noisy and denoised images. Thisstudy not only offers a comprehensive approach to addressing the challenges of image denoising in medical imaging but alsohas significant societal benefits. By improving the clarity of images used in Alzheimer's research, the study contributes to more accurate diagnoses and better understanding of the disease, potentially leading to improved patient outcomes and advancing public health efforts in combating Alzheimer's disease.

articleTitle: Implementation of Machine Learning Algorithms to Detect DoS Attack in WSN
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive work on the detection of Denial of Service (DoS) attacks in Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) using machine learning algorithms. It provides an overview of WSNs, the nature of DoS attacks, and the specific challenges of DoS attacks in WSN environments. Utilizing the WSN-DS dataset, the implementation includes data preprocessing techniques such as Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Min-Max Scaling. The approach uses Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and XGBoost algorithms forming four combination algorithms: CNN coupled with PCA, CNN, XGBoost with PCA, and XGBoost to classify and detect DoS attacks. Among the models tested, XGBoost with Min-Max Scaling demonstrated superior accuracy of 99.7% compared to the other models.

articleTitle: Virtual Instrumentation under Supervisory Control for Safe Water Level Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: Water supplies are essential to farming and agriculture productivity as well as to our standard of living. Traditional water supply and quality monitoring systems need a large workforce in addition to complicated infrastructure. Agriculture depends heavily on the ability to control the level of water of a water supply, such as a water tank, bore well, etc It is difficult to monitor water tanks in real time using traditional water distribution methods. We can adjust to the newest technology in order to remove the complexity and streamline the system. For the water level monitoring system, a PID Control scheme that is solely software-oriented is thus created using LabVIEW.The Internet of Things (IoT) concept is used for continuous monitoring. In addition to tracking usage and gathering data via Wi-Fi and LAN, the server also keeps an eye on how much water is wasted at each outlet due to overuse. An alert is mailed to the user to let them know when water usage exceeds a predetermined level. With the help of this, customers can utilise a laptop or mobile device with an internet connection to continuously monitor water levels To prevent hacking, it additionally offers verified user access to this system. The government and authorities may monitor and manage the water supply with the help of this suggested water level monitoring system, which also enables individuals, schools, hospitals, businesses, department stores, malls, and agricultural areas to keep track of how much water they waste.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Hybrid Hierarchical Routing Protocol for Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: Primarily employed to achieve this objective, wireless sensor networks (WSNs) are designed to track environmental or physical conditions. They obtain data from their environment efficiently and deliver it all at once to a specific location. The main issues are network longevity, usage of energy, and coordinated transmission, even though their efficacy is well established. This study proposes a unique approach to improve network endurance and address these issues. The technique seeks to improve WSN performance as a whole. In particular, a hybrid hierarchical routing system is presented to address problems with the current protocols, such as excessive energy usage in addition to high latency. For boosting the longevity of the WSN, the primary goals are to lower intra-cluster transmission and limit contact with base station. To lower quantity of energy spent while distributing to distant base stations (BS), the suggested approach encompasses gateway nodes, hybrid time synchronization, locality-sensitive hashing (LSH) based data aggregation technique, and cluster choice focused on centrality. To demonstrate effectiveness of the presented technique, a comparison with a traditional method is carried out, assessing several performance indicators. In regards to gauges of performance including latency, throughput, total dead nodes, network energy consumption, and data packets transmitted, hybrid approach outperforms conventional approaches.

articleTitle: Estimation of Respiratory Rate Using Thermography
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: This study explores the application of infrared thermography for non-contact monitoring of human respiratory rate. Using a passive thermography approach, the study presents a non-invasive method utilizing thermal images, enabling continuous and remote respiratory rate monitoring without radiation exposure. Thermography's ability to detect changes in respiratory rate patterns can indicate various health conditions, often capturing early signs before clinical manifestation. Additionally, in driver monitoring systems, integrating low-level bio vitals like heart rate and respiratory rate with visual cues from cameras enhances road safety by enabling early detection of drowsiness. The study highlights various respiratory rate measurement methods, and its proposed methodology involves collecting data from healthy subjects using a handheld thermal imaging camera, processing thermal images to detect the nose region, and analysing temperature variations to derive respiratory rate signals. Validation against accelerometer data demonstrates promising accuracy, offering potential clinical applications as a non-invasive and accurate respiratory rate monitoring approach.

articleTitle: Automating the Optimal Temperature to Increase the Yield in Sericulture by Using Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: Sericulture/, the art of cultivating silk through the rearing of silkworms, earns its title as the Queen of Textiles owing to its unmatched softness, elegance, durability, and tensile strength. India, the second-largest producer of silk, favors this luxurious fabric for its exceptional water absorbency, heat resistance, and inherent luster. The intricacies of insect adaptation, particularly evident in mulberry silkworms, underscore the significance of maintaining optimal temperature and humidity levels, factors pivotal for their growth and survival. However, conventional methods of temperature regulation, such as employing wetted gunny bags, are insufficient for the precise monitoring demanded by sericulture. In this paper, a model has been proposed to revolutionize sericulture management by leveraging IoT and cloud technologies to ensure real-time monitoring of temperature and humidity within silkworm sheds. By offering insights into the interplay of humidity, airflow, and light on silkworm development, this system aims to enhance cocoon crop yields while minimizing the need for manual oversight. This holistic approach guarantees the production of superior-quality silk with consistent characteristics, heralding a new era of efficiency and excellence in the silk industry.

articleTitle: Smart Cart: Revolutionizing E-Commerce in India with AI-Powered Personalized Product Recommendations Overview
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: The rapid evolution of e-commerce has intensified the need for effective personalization to enhance user experience. This paper introduces SmartCart, an innovative website that integrates cutting-edge AI technologies to provide personalized product recommendations based on image uploads. Users can interact with the platform by uploading images of products they like and selecting from various AI models designed for different recommendation tasks. These models include convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for image similarity analysis and generative adversarial networks (GANs) for contextual product suggestions. SmartCart leverages these technologies to offer highly relevant and visually similar product recommendations, aiming to improve user satisfaction and engagement. Despite its advancements, SmartCart faces limitations inherent to AI in e-commerce. Challenges such as the variability in image quality, the need for extensive training data, and potential biases in model predictions can impact the accuracy and relevance of recommendations. Additionally, the system's effectiveness is constrained by the diversity of user preferences and the capability of AI models to generalize across different product categories. This paper explores how SmartCart addresses these challenges and discusses future directions for improving AI-driven recommendation systems in the context of e-commerce.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Powered Authentication and Supply Chain Integration to Combat Counterfeit Drugs
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: Counterfeit drugs pose a significant threat to public health and undermine the integrity of pharmaceutical supply chains globally. This research explores a novel application of blockchain technology to authenticate pharmaceutical products and enhance transparency for end users. Although blockchain has been utilized in pharmaceutical supply chains, our study introduces an innovative approach focusing on blockchain-powered authentication mechanisms, such as unique identifiers and cryptographic verification. These mechanisms enable end users to verify the product authenticity of the drug by entering provided identifiers on the company's application. If the identifier fails to display the expected information, it indicates that the product may be counterfeit. Moreover, users can access comprehensive details about the product's journey, including manufacturing, storage conditions, and distribution, promoting transparency and trust. The displayed information is securely extracted from the blockchain-driven supply chain, ensuring data integrity and authenticity, while confidential data remains protected. Through an in-depth analysis of literature, case studies, and implementation strategies, this research demonstrates the potential of blockchain-driven solutions to mitigate counterfeit drug risks. The findings highlight the importance of stakeholder collaboration in leveraging blockchain technology for authentication and transparency, ultimately safeguarding public health and building trust with end users.

articleTitle: Secure Skies: Developing a Remotely Piloted Aerial System with Defense Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: The Remotely Piloted Air Defense System (RPAS) represents an innovative advancement in security technology, integrating cutting-edge components for precise operation and enhanced security. This system features a user-friendly web interface designed for seamless remote control and monitoring, bolstered by intuitive UI/UX design and efficient communication with air traffic controllers. CAD-optimized airframe design ensures optimal balance in weight, strength, and aerodynamics. Rigorous testing across individual modules and integrated deployment has validated system performance, including successful deployment of the protection mechanism. Future iterations aim to further enhance target detection, fortify defenses, and integrate advanced analytics. This project highlights the transformative potential of unmanned aerial systems in critical sectors, emphasizing safety, security, and efficiency through innovative technology.

articleTitle: QCVNET - Leveraging Quantum Technology in Convolutional Neural Networks for Improved Cardiovascular Disease Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: The primary issue of global health today is Cardio-vascular diseases (CVDs) and thus requires accurate predictive models for detecting it early. Quantum technology combined with regular deep learning techniques are used by researchers here to improve the accuracy of forecast on heart diseases. While using an expanded dataset with clinical and demographic records, an innovative approach was found to use Quantum Convolutional Neural Network (QCVNET) structure that merged quantum layers into classical CNN framework with Principal Component Analysis (PCA) that allowed for consistency of features with respect to the quantum bits' number. The performance of the QCVNET was evaluated by comparing it to Quantum LSTM, Quantum DNN, Quantum GRU, and Quantum RNN, which are other quantum models enhanced with conventional neural networks, and other traditional non-quantum models like SVM, RF, RNN and DNN, using different indicators of quality like f1-score or recall. In early CVD prediction, the QCVNET model produced an impressive accuracy of 91.73%, beating all other models, showcasing the potential impact of quantum-enhanced deep learning for timely diagnosis and personalized treatment strategies while providing means to reduce the global burden of cardiovascular diseases.

articleTitle: HQI-GAN: Improved High Quality Image GAN to Resolve Low Resolution Quality Images
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: The rapid evolution of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has significantly impacted the field of image processing, especially in tasks involving super-resolution. This proposal introduces HQI-GAN, an innovative framework specifically designed to enhance low-resolution images through the advanced capabilities of GANs. HQI-GAN seeks to overcome the difficulties associated with restoring degraded image content, which often presents challenges for traditional methods due to the intricate details and sharp edges found in images. The framework utilizes a specialized generative network architecture that includes a generator, a discriminator, and an adversarial loss function, all working in tandem to produce images of superior quality while maintaining the clarity and accuracy of the original content. By integrating adversarial training with the latest techniques in high-resolution imaging, HQI-GAN is capable of generating highly detailed and visually appealing reconstructions of low-resolution images. Extensive testing and evaluation reveal that HQI-GAN outperforms existing methods, particularly in improving the quality and readability of low-resolution text images. The results demonstrate HQI-GAN's effectiveness in achieving its goals, positioning it as a valuable contribution to the image processing field and high-resolution image enhancement.

articleTitle: Concatenated Polar and Non binary LDPC codes for High Reliability in Optical Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: Next-generation high-speed optical transport systems require powerful forward error correction (FEC) codes with high error-correcting capabilities to ensure high data reliability. Low density parity check (LDPC) codes are strong candidates for ensuring the high data reliability needed to support data rates of 100 Gb/s, demanded by optical systems. Non-binary LDPC (NB-LDPC) codes provides better performance compared to binary version, as they offer larger coding gains with shorter code lengths and reduced system latency. Despite their advantages, LDPC codes suffer from error floor problem at low bit error rates (BER), with NB-LDPC codes showing error floors at BER around 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-7</sup>. High-speed optical transport systems generally require BERs of the order of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-12</sup>. The error floor problem can be mitigated by concatenating LDPC codes with a shorter outer code. Existing works mainly focus on employing Reed Solomon (RS) codes to remove error floor. However, the decoding complexity is high for these codes. This paper proposes concatenated Polar and NB-LDPC codes to address the error floor issue, since polar codes have relatively low encoding and decoding complexity. The channel noise in optical communication systems using optical amplifiers cannot be analyzed using simplified additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN). Hence the channel noise is mathematically derived and proved that chi-square channel model is appropriate than AWGN. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed concatenated codes over proposed channel model can achieve a net coding gain of around 1.5dB at a BER of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-12</sup>.

articleTitle: Classification of Ovarian Cancer with Multimodal Data Using AI Technology– A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: One of the main causes of carcinoma includes ovarian epithelial cells. To monitor the ovarian cancer., there are number of approaches such as biomarkers., ultrasound scan., Histopathology., CT scan etc. Artificial Intelligence (AI) contributes a important function in the area of medical sciences that operates on different modalities and helps the doctor to provide timely treatment. Deep learning models are operative to integrate different modalities which help to upsurge the accuracy for both diagnosis and prognosis. AI models are also proficient to notice the pattern which describes patient responses towards the treatment. In this work deep learning architecture are incorporated for accurate and initial finding of the cancer by integration multiple modalities such as biomarkers and histopathological images. Algorithms for machine learning work well in differentiating between patients with aggressive and benign ovarian cancer. Statistical analysis can be accomplished to compute the risk factor and the survival period of the patient. So by these techniques it is helpful to notice the epithelial ovarian cancer at early stage before it spreads to other organs.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Readout Electronics for Thermopile Array Detector Using FPGA
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: Thermopile detector arrays, integral to infrared sensors, find widespread application in temperature measurement and thermal imaging. This paper introduces a novel approach by designing dedicated readout electronics for thermopile detectors, aiming at their characterization for space applications, specifically in a safe mode earth sensor. The proposed system employs a reprogrammable Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) for implementing the readout electronics, encompassing tasks such as extracting raw pixel data from the detector and configuring the sensor for different parameter settings. The safe mode earth sensor, crucial for spacecraft attitude determination, provides 2-axes attitude referencing Earth in the pitch and roll axes. Leveraging thermopile-based earth sensors, the system detects Earth edges in the IR band, facilitating the calculation of roll and pitch angles. The compact design makes it particularly suitable for deployment in Micro-Satellites and other satellites as a safe mode sensor. The readout electronics and data acquisition system play a pivotal role in evaluating, characterizing, and screening thermopile detectors, ensuring their suitability for deployment in safe mode earth sensor applications. This integrated approach not only enhances the efficiency of thermopile detectors but also opens avenues for their broader application in space-based sensing systems.

articleTitle: Design of Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulator Machine for Chronic Low Back Pain
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: Using electrical current to stimulate and excite a living body's nervous system is known as Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation(TENS). The word electrotherapy has been used to describe a wide range of medical procedures, including shock therapy and the use of devices like deep brain stimulators for neurological disorders. The use of electrical current to accelerate the process of healing of wounds has also been included in this definition. This treatment also belongs to alternative medications in particularly for spinal cord and remedies because it is non-pharmacological. It acts as a nonphar-macological therapy that minimizes hyperalgesia by descending inhibitory mechanisms in the nervous system's center, which in turn stimulates a complicated neural network that decreases pain. To control pain, TENS devices apply electrical current through electrodes applied to the skin to provide a non-invasive nerve stimulation system that can reduce acute and chronic pain. This paper describes the development, implementation, and maintenance of a system that may be used to treat illnesses at a relatively low cost. The user can also vary the system's frequency from low to high depending on the intended purpose.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis of Movie Reviews in Regional Language: Kannada
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: Sentiment analysis is the process of gathering and examining people's thoughts, feelings, attitudes, views, etc. about various subjects, goods, and services. The rapid development of applications such as YonTube, Instagram, Twitter and Facebook, and web pages encourages people to create a vast amount of reviews and comments regarding daily activities, goods, and services. Businesses, governments and researchers can use sentiment analysis as a potential tool to gather and examine public opinion and mood in order to obtain business intelligence and improve decision-making. Kannada language has been taken here as resources are very less on the internet. In this study, Movie reviews were collected in English language from IMDb website and translated into Kannada using deep translator for translation. First emojis and punctuation are removed then text is tokenized and sent to 2 BiLSTM (Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory) layers. Then they are fed into many Fully Connected layers and a softmax activation function. The proposed model is compared with other deep learning models such as BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Trans formers) and DistilBERT. The performance of the proposed model is analyzed in terms of accuracy. Considering the accuracies of the models being BERT (0.616), DistilBERT (0.67) and Multilingual Representations for Indian Languages(MuRIL) (0.690), MuRIL was a better choice building the base model for the study than the other two counterparts.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis Using Natural Language Processing, Machine Learning and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: Sentiment analysis is a vital branch of Natural Language Processing (NLP) that identifies the emotions expressed in a text. In this study, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks perform a unique sentiment analysis on data gathered from the Twitter site. This work intends to determine the performance of temporal models such as LSTMs in sentiment analysis tasks using many tweets from the Sentiment 140 dataset, which consists of 1.6 million tagged tweets. Following extensive pre-processing and creating the best possible LSTM model architecture, the model produced an astounding mean accuracy of almost 84 percent. Techniques like noise removal, tokenization, and removing stop words are used in pre-processing. Once the data is pre-processed, the required feature extraction is done using the GloVe embedding technique. Then, various machine learning models, like KNN, SVM, decision tree, and random forest, were built, along with a deep learning model using LSTM. These models are further evaluated using accuracy, precision, and recall metrics. The test set findings showed a considerable improvement, indicating a 15.53% increase in accuracy, a 16.56% increase in Precision, and a 13.31% increase in Recall compared to previously built Machine Learning models. This significant improvement demonstrates LSTM networks' capacity to detect and understand temporal relationships in textual data, confirming its efficacy in sentiment analysis. The study's conclusions demonstrate how LSTM networks can improve sentiment analysis tasks by offering a solid foundation for deciphering and interpreting subtle emotional differences in social media data.

articleTitle: A Multimodal Approach to Detect Driver Drowsiness
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: Driver fatigue, manifesting as drowsiness and loss of concentration, poses a significant risk to road safety. We present a novel real-time approach for detecting driver fatigue by combining feature recognition, head pose estimation, and eye gaze tracking. Utilizing 3D landmarks from the MediaPipe framework, our method provides a comprehensive assessment of driver alertness in both real-world and controlled environments. Our system leverages the YOLOv5 algorithm for feature recognition to extract crucial driver cues and employs advanced 3D facial landmarks from MediaPipe for precise head and eye position estimation. This multimodal approach effectively evaluates driver concentration and alertness, focusing on critical fatigue indicators such as drowsiness and yawning. The face mesh, with 468 facial landmarks, calculates head position, eye position, and blink patterns to accurately identify signs of sleepiness. A total of 17 subjects participated in the data collection, driving the car under various lighting conditions and 13 subjects for in lab data collection under different lighting conditions. This diverse dataset was instrumental in training and testing the model, ensuring its robustness and adaptability to real-world scenarios. By integrating these techniques, our approach offers robust detection of driver fatigue and concentration levels, enhancing road safety.

articleTitle: Advancing Heart Disease Prediction: A Hybrid Approach Integrating Machine Learning and Clinical Expertise
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: Globally, cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) remain the primary cause of illness and deaths. Healthcare providers must be able to anticipate the onset of these diseases in order to make well-informed decisions about the diagnosis, treatment, and care of their patients. Thus, Machine learning (ML) models have become powerful tools in this context by offering the potential to identify critical risk factors and enhance the diagnostic process related to heart disease. The primary objective of this work is to leverage machine learning techniques to improve the prediction accuracy of heart disease. By identifying the most significant features through feature selection techniques, the study aims to enhance the predictive capability of the models. Furthermore, the research develops the possibility of building a hybrid model by merging the top two models based on their evaluation metrics. By using this hybrid model, the prediction of cardiovascular diseases should be greatly enhanced. Healthcare professionals can potentially avert the onset of severe cardiac events by appropriately identifying patients who are at high risk and taking preventative action. Additionally, this work adds to the ongoing efforts to create trustworthy and accurate algorithms for the prediction of cardiovascular disease, which is crucial for bettering patient outcomes and lowering the prevalence of heart disease worldwide. This method advances preventive healthcare and personalized medicine, which is a larger objective, in addition to increasing prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Non-Stationary Blind Source Separation and Advanced Signal Processing Techniques for Effective Fetal ECG Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: Fetal electrocardiogram (FECG) extraction from maternal electrocardiogram (MECG) signals presents a major obstacle in biomedical signal processing. In this paper Fast Independent Subspace Analysis (FastISA), Fast Independent Component Analysis (FastICA) and Join Approximate Diagonalization of Eigen Matrices(JADE) is used as for Blind Source Separation (BSS) with stern pre-processing steps like band pass filtering, wavelet denoising, orthogonalization and Wiener deconvolution. To evaluate the quality of separation Amari Index has been implemented achieving 0.19 for synthetic data using fastISA and 0.33 for real-world using JADE algorithm providing reliable operation for different situations as FECG extraction is crucial for its insights on fetal hearts electrical activity with non-invasive means to monitor and diagnose early during pregnancy. A predictive model based on Random Forest and a Neural Network along with R Peak Detection based on Pan-Tompkins algorithm has been implemented to predict pregnancy states and physiological metric for analyzing Mothers Health condition. Integration of predictive model and Signal processing techniques like FastISA and Pan-Tompkins algorithm provides a wider application of this approach in biomedical engineering for improved healthcare and diagnostics.

articleTitle: Implementation and Extension of Bit Manipulation Instruction on RISC-V Architecture using FPGA
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: The inclusion of Bit Manipulation Instructions (BMIs) has become more and more important as embedded systems continue to demand optimum performance together with a good energy economy. Although BMIs have been adopted by x86 and ARMv8 architectures to improve runtime efficiency and reduce power consumption, the RISC-V platform-which is preferred for its adaptability in embedded applications-has not been as successful in this area. Ten improved BMIs designed specifically for the RISC-V Instruction Set Architecture (ISA) are proposed in this work to close this gap. We synthesized a superior RISC-V architecture for the Zynq Board FPGA and TSMC 3nm platforms implementing the TSMC 3nm cell library. Initial assessments of software also show conceivable enhancements, especially in power-hungry and time-consuming cryptographic applications. Our work draws attention to low cost and power consumption while the principles of high performance and security prerequisites therefore deal with the urgent need for energy-efficient computing solutions in consumer electronics with the introduction of these advanced BMIs. By adopting the built-in benefits of RISC-VISA in conjunction with customized BMI extensions, we offer a feasible plan for the development of effective embedded systems that provide more computing power.

articleTitle: SmartGuard: A Proactive Surveillance System for Enhancing Security in Transportation Hubs
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: Ensuring security within transportation hubs re-mains a paramount concern in contemporary society. The ever-evolving landscape of security threats necessitates innovative solutions to safeguard public safety effectively. This paper introduces SmartGuard, a proactive surveillance system designed to address the critical challenge of detecting unattended objects in transportation hubs. Leveraging cutting-edge technologies such as advanced sensors and artificial intelligence, SmartGuard aims to provide real-time threat analysis and minimize potential risks, including explosives or hazardous materials. By surpassing the limitations of traditional security systems, SmartGuard heralds a new era of resilient security practices, significantly enhancing the safety of public transit environments.

articleTitle: Secure ML Based Image Encryption Framework with Recursive Splitting and Linear Feedback Shift Register
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: With the development of advanced communication ensuring the secure transmission of images has become more and more important. This research suggests a novel approach for digital image encryption and decryption that combines Linear Feedback Shift Register (LFSR) encryption, recursive image splitting and shuffling in order to increase security. Test image is divided into blocks and each block is encrypted using a different LFSR key. The encrypted blocks are then joined to create a single encrypted image that is ready to be sent. The receiver uses a machine learning model that has been pre-trained to identify the specific LFSR key used for each block after breaking the image back up into its component blocks. This allows for precise decryption. The viability of the encryption process is assessed using entropy analysis, histogram comparison and pixel relationship etc. The results show that the encrypted images have a notable disruption of spatial relationships, a high degree of unpredictability, and significant interference with spatial relations. Furthermore, evaluation is done on the performance of multiple Support Vector Machine (SVM) models with different kernel functions. The results indicate that the SVM with a radial basis function (RBF) kernel performs best in terms of key identification accuracy. This thorough analysis demonstrates the suggested encryption method's resilience and its potential for safe image transfer across a range of applications.

articleTitle: Detection and Classification of Fish Using Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: Aquaculture, also known as aqua farming, plays a substantial role in India's agricultural industry. India is a major global fish producer, with aquaculture playing a significant role in the country's economy, food security, and jobs. India's varied climatic conditions and abundant water resources, such as rivers, ponds, lakes, and coastal regions, make it a very suitable place for aquaculture. The enhancement of the maritime economy relies on the accurate detection and identification of marine species. Accurate detection of aquatic species thriving in a demanding marine environment can be benefit the local as well as researchers. This research study proposes a framework for a YOLOv8, YOLOv9, ResNet50, Vgg19, DenseNet201 convolutional neural network that is specifically trained on aquatic marine life. This study used a variety of nine distinct marine animals, including fish, Black-sea sprat, Gilt head bream, Horse mackerel, Red-mullet, Red-sea bream, Sea bass, Shrimp, Stripped red mullet and Trout. When detection model is executed, it found that YOLOv9 performs better than YOLOv8. This research work reveals that in terms of classification of fish species it was found that ResNet50 has higher efficiency compared to YOLOv8, Vgg19, DenseNet201.

articleTitle: Study of Memristor Based Logic Gates Performance and Comparing with CMOS Realization
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: Energy-efficient and high-performance electronic devices lead to exploring alternatives to traditional CMOS circuits. Memristor-based logic gates, such as basic gates (NOT, AND, OR), universal gates (NAND, NOR), and arithmetic gates (XOR, XNOR), are implemented and compared with CMOS counterparts. The memristor is a parasitic device and non-volatility that is used in memories, logic gates, and neuromorphic systems. The memristor changes its resistance with an applied voltage, switching between high-resistance and low-resistance states. The memristor gate designs have an evident potential for faster switching speeds, power, and better noise margin (NM) enhancement. The integration of memristors with CMOS technology may leads to hybrid architectures that optimize both speed and power efficiency.

articleTitle: Adaptive Contrast Based Real-Time Image and Video Dehazing
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Circuits, Control, Communication and Computing (I4C)
abstract: Dehazing algorithms have been developed in re-sponse to the need for effectively and instantaneously removing atmospheric turbidities such as mist, haze, and fog from media. The removal of haze from an image or video enables the extraction of additional details from the scene. This paper presents the development of a real-time, memory-optimized dehazing system that utilizes digital image processing techniques and NVIDIA's CUDA architecture for efficient parallel computing. The methodology incorporates a quad-tree search algorithm for efficient atmospheric light estimation, which significantly enhances dehazing accuracy. Advanced contrast enhancement techniques are employed for transmission estimation to ensure clarity and visibility in dehazed images, addressing challenges such as non-uniform illumination and varying haze densities. For image restoration, the system dynamically clips values to improve brightness and minimize information loss. The transmission map's artifacts are then smoothed using a Gaussian filter, resulting in more reliable dehazing. Extensive testing on a variety of publicly accessible datasets demonstrated that the proposed model achieved comparable accuracy to numerous existing techniques, while also restoring high-quality dehazed images and videos. The system achieves a running time of 35ms per image and up to 10ms per frame for video sequences. Performance was objectively assessed using the Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) and Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM), yielding a PSNR of 28.75 and an SSIM of 0.80.
